speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. Can you tell me more about your skin lesions and how long you've had the fever and wrist pain?

speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old male. The patient presents with a 3-day history of pain in his left wrist, which worsened this morning accompanied by chills and malaise. He recounts having a self-resolving left knee pain the previous week. Reports recent return from a camping trip in Minnesota. Sexually active with one female partner. No history of trauma to the wrist.

speaker: Doctor
text: Have you noticed any red, expanding skin patches or a rash on your body, particularly on your wrists or ankles? Also, have you been bitten by any ticks while camping in Minnesota?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Pain in the left wrist. I also have Chills, Malaise, Painless violaceous vesiculopustular lesions on both wrists and hands, Swelling and erythema of the left wrist, Severe tenderness to palpation and passive movement of the left wrist.

speaker: Doctor
text: The combination of recent camping in Minnesota, migratory arthritis, and violaceous vesiculopustular lesions on the hands is highly specific. DIAGNOSIS READY: Erythema Migrans with secondary Lyme disease manifestations, specifically Borrelial Lymphocytoma or early disseminated Lyme arthritis.
